podcast.title: Distinguished Scientific Career
podcast.body: Brian Cox has gone on to hold several prestigious scientific chairs, authored a number of books, and is a well-known host of science shows for the BBC, cementing his career as a full-time physicist. "Since then, he's been a full on physicist, even working at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in Switzerland."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Physicist and Academic
podcast.body: While playing keyboards for the dance act D:Ream (referred to as "Dream" in the transcript), Brian Cox studied physics at the University of Manchester. After the band ended in 1997, he continued his education, earning a doctorate in philosophy and working in high-energy particle physics, including at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in Switzerland. "When he was playing keyboards with them, he studied physics at the University of Manchester."

xref.title: Band Disbanded in 1997
xref.body: The dance act D:Ream, which featured Brian Cox on keyboards, ended in 1997. "When the band died in 1997, he continued with his education earning a doctorate in philosophy and working with high energy particle physics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Brian Cox's Parallel Careers
xref.body: In the early 1990s, Brian Cox was a keyboardist in the electro-pop band Dream while simultaneously pursuing his PhD in physics. He is now Professor Brian Cox, a prominent British scientist involved with the Large Hadron Collider in Switzerland. "Back in the early 90s, Brian played keyboards in an electro pop band called Dream."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
